# Member Appeal — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date I am sending this letter]

**To:** Aetna — Member Complaint and Appeal Unit
**Submitted via:** Aetna Member Complaint and Appeal Form (aetna.com, under complaints, grievances and appeals), by fax to 859‑425‑3379 or by mail to the appeal address printed on my denial letter
**Appeal must be received by:** 2027‑01‑31

**From:**
Quinn Jennings
Member ID: W670697505
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

**RE: Appeal of adverse benefit determination dated 2026‑08‑04 — Reference number POC‑6E16FAD700‑45453**
**Service denied:** Bunion surgery (hallux valgus), CPT 28296
**Governing policy:** Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy (https://www.aetna.com/cpb/medical/data/600_699/0629.html)

---

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for bunion surgery (CPT 28296), which Aetna issued on 2026‑08‑04 under reference number POC‑6E16FAD700‑45453. The notice states that the documentation submitted was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I am asking Aetna to reconsider that decision, and I am writing this appeal to lay out, point by point, where each element the plan's own policy asks for appears in my records.

My surgeon, Dr. Duval, MD (orthopedic surgery), has documented that this procedure is needed. The criteria below are quoted word for word from Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy, the plan's own published policy.

## The plan's criteria, matched to my records

**1. The plan's general medical necessity framing.**

The policy states:

> "Medical Necessity Aetna considers the following interventions medically necessary:"

and

> "Members with clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management who meet the following criteria:"

My record shows both clinical symptoms and a history of conservative management. I have had 24 months of progressive pain in the foot, unrelieved by rest.

**2. The requested surgery is the category of surgery the policy describes.**

The policy states:

> "Bony Correction Bunionectomy Bony correction bunionectomy (e.g., Akin, Chevron, Keller, Lapidus, Mitchell, proximal metatarsal osteotomy procedures, etc.) to treat symptomatic hallux valgus (bunion) in a skeletally mature individual (i.e., after epiphyseal closure) or an individual who is 18 years of age or older when the following criteria is met:"

I am an adult over 18. The requested procedure, CPT 28296, is a bony correction bunionectomy to treat symptomatic hallux valgus. My weight‑bearing foot radiographs of 2026‑06‑29 document a hallux valgus angle of 38 degrees and an intermetatarsal angle of 17 degrees — confirming the diagnosis the policy addresses.

**3. Persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment.**

The policy states:

> "Documentation of persistent pain and difficulty walking despite at least six months of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional which includes, but may not be limited to:"

and

> "The member's pain and symptoms over the medial bony eminence or calluses persist, making walking difficult despite at least a 6-month trial of conservative treatment under the direction of a healthcare professional that includes the following:"

My conservative treatment has been directed by healthcare professionals and is documented as follows:

| What the policy lists | What my records document |
|---|---|
| "Shoe inserts (generally contractually excluded);" | Wide toe‑box footwear and a custom orthotic, together with activity modification, over 10 weeks from 2026‑04‑12 to 2026‑06‑21, 18 visits completed, recorded in the physical therapy discharge note |
| "Corticosteroid injections;" | Corticosteroid injection on 2026‑03‑25, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief |
| Conservative measures generally — "According to accepted guidelines, treatment should initially consist of conservative measures;" | NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief |

My symptoms have persisted through all of it. My records state that I cannot tolerate closed shoes and that there is ulceration risk over the prominence. On examination, provocative testing was positive on the affected side and my range of motion is limited by pain. My pain has continued for 24 months and is unrelieved by rest.

I want to be precise about one point rather than overstate it: the physical therapy course itself ran 10 weeks. My overall non‑surgical treatment, however, spans more than six months under professional direction — NSAIDs for 6 months, the corticosteroid injection on 2026‑03‑25, and the footwear, orthotic and activity‑modification program that ran from 2026‑04‑12 to 2026‑06‑21 — against a 24‑month symptom history. If Aetna reads any part of this sequence as not meeting the six‑month threshold, I ask that the specific gap be identified in writing so it can be addressed.

**4. The requested procedure is consistent with how the policy reserves fusion.**

The policy states:

> "Fusion is the procedure of choice for hallux valgus associated with advanced degenerative joint disease, and advanced hallux valgus (IMA greater than 20 degrees, HVA greater than 40 degrees), severely subluxated or dislocated MTP joints, or for failed hallux valgus surgery."

It also states:

> "Arthrodesis or a Keller procedure is the generally accepted treatment of choice following failed cheilectomy or where advanced degenerative changes are present."

and

> "Another indication for arthrodesis includes a failed Keller bunionectomy."

My measured angles — IMA 17 degrees and HVA 38 degrees — fall below the thresholds the policy associates with fusion, and my records do not describe prior hallux valgus surgery or a prior cheilectomy. A bony correction bunionectomy, not a fusion, is therefore the procedure that matches my findings under the plan's own framework.

**5. Follow-up.**

The policy states:

> "Minimum follow-up was at least 12 months."

I understand this from the policy's discussion of published outcomes rather than as something I could have completed before surgery. My surgeon's office has arranged post‑operative follow‑up, and I am willing to complete whatever follow‑up schedule Dr. Duval directs.

## Other clinical facts in my record

My records also document no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and that I am a non‑smoker.

## What I am asking for

The denial says my documentation was incomplete. The records summarized above address the diagnosis, the symptom history, the failed conservative measures, the imaging measurements, the physical examination findings and the functional limitation. I ask Aetna to:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026‑08‑04 (reference POC‑6E16FAD700‑45453) and authorize CPT 28296; or
2. If any single element is still considered missing, tell me in writing exactly which criterion in Aetna CPB 0629 – Bunionectomy is unmet and what specific document would satisfy it, so my surgeon's office can send it.

I also request that this appeal be reviewed by a physician with expertise in orthopedic foot and ankle surgery, and I ask for a copy of the specific criteria and any internal guideline relied on in making this determination.

I am attaching: [list of records being enclosed — e.g., physical therapy discharge note, radiology report of 2026‑06‑29, office notes from Dr. Duval, injection record of 2026‑03‑25]. Please contact me at [my phone number] or my surgeon's office at [surgeon's office phone number] if anything further is needed.

Thank you for taking another look at this.

Sincerely,

**Quinn Jennings**
Member ID: W670697505
[Signature]
[Date]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
